title: Taking up saxophone in Chicago; saxophone in New Orleans
summary: Inspired by the Six Brown Brothers, his group bought saxophones at the Stratford Hotel; saxophone was uncommon in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Baritone horn. Mm-hmm. I wondered about the saxophone when you were a boy there, or young, I don't mean by a boy five years old, but I mean up to the...
I didn't start the saxophone until I came here to Stratford Hotel.
At that time, if you remember the Brown Brothers here in Vaudeville?

Well, we decided we'd all take up saxophones. And we went over to Conn and bought a whole set of saxophones. And we had one of the men, the only, at that time, the only tenor saxophone player we had among our group, happened to be working with us. And he was our instructor. And we bought these saxophones. We had a baritone. We had a tenor. Two altos. And after a few lessons, we developed a couple of quartets. And during the dinner hour, we used to lay down these regular instruments and then play saxophone quartets, imitating the Brown Brothers. And of course, everybody liked it so well, we just stayed with it.
Did they use the saxophone very much in New Orleans, if you can remember?
Or the big brass bands, do you remember? Or say the lyric band, they wouldn't have used anything.
Of course there, but I mean the other bands.
No, the saxophone came into popularity much, much later than that.
I think they say the saxophone was invented by a Frenchman or from Belgium.
By the name of Sax. Aldo. Yes, Adolf Sax.
So you would think that if it were a French...
It's a development from an instrument that was called a sax, but... Oh yes, I remember.
